title: Dimension of a finite type domain over a field equals the transcendence degree of its fraction field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is an integral domain. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be its fraction field. Then the Krull dimension of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and the transcendence degree of $K$ over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] are finite and equal: $$\dim A=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K.$$ Moreover, for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$, the local ring $A_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] has this same dimension.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P0 (label lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring, lines 28171-28191); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00P0,algebra-lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring)

proof.text: Write $A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/\mathfrak p$, where $\mathfrak p$ is prime because $A$ is a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] (Algebra 00OS), $\dim A$ is a finite non-negative integer and $\dim A_{\mathfrak m}=\dim A$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. This proves the local-ring assertion, leaving the comparison with transcendence degree.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00P0 (lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring), first two sentences: the source invokes Lemma 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring); the cited 00OS node states the needed local-dimension consequence, proved from 00OR

proof.text: By Noether normalization [lem-weil-pbc-noether-normalization-field] (Algebra 00OY), there are $d\ge0$ and an injective $k$-algebra map $P=k[Y_1,\ldots,Y_d]\hookrightarrow A$ such that $A$ is a finite $P$-module. The finite ring map is integral [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] gives $\dim A=\dim P$. The polynomial ring $P$ is a finite type domain over $k$, hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] identifies its dimension with that of the localization at the maximal ideal $(Y_1,\ldots,Y_d)$; [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] computes the latter as $d$. Thus $d=\dim A$, the dimension clause of 00OY. Write $y_i$ for the images of $Y_i$; their algebraic independence follows from injectivity.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00P0, 'Apply Lemma [00OY]. We get a finite injective ring map ... with d = dim(S)'

proof.text: Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(P)=k(y_1,\ldots,y_d)\subseteq K$. Localizing the finite $P$-module $A$ at $P\setminus\{0\}$ gives a finite-dimensional $F$-algebra $B=F\otimes_PA$; it remains a nonzero domain because $P\hookrightarrow A$ and $A$ is a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], $B$ is a field. It contains $A$, and each element of $B$ is a fraction $a/s$ with $a\in A$ and $0\ne s\in P$; thus $B\subseteq K$, while, being a field containing $A$, it contains $K$. Hence $B=K$ and $K/F$ is finite-dimensional, therefore algebraic.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00P0, 'Clearly, k(y_1, ..., y_d) subset K is a finite extension' (finite-module localization expanded)

proof.text: The $y_i$ are algebraically independent over $k$ (Step 2), and $K$ is algebraic over $k(y_1,\ldots,y_d)$ (Step 3). Thus $(y_1,\ldots,y_d)$ is a transcendence basis of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. By the cardinality clause of [def-kun-transcendence-degree], $\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=d=\dim A$; Step 1 gives the same value for every $A_{\mathfrak m}$.
